beliefs.practice: Read the connection URI only from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or commit it. Provide a .env.example with a placeholder value.
Create a single MongoClient/connection and reuse it as a process-wide singleton (do not open a new client per request).
Require TLS/SSL for connections and verify server certificates (use the w=ssl or tls options appropriate to your driver) and avoid disabling certificate validation.
Store production DB credentials in a secure secret store (Azure Key Vault) and load them at runtime instead of environment variables for long-lived production secrets.

Use least-privilege database users: create a user/role limited to the sample_customer_360_08 database with only the permissions required (read, write on specific collections), do not use the cluster admin key for the app.
Protect the cluster by restricting network access: enable firewall rules/VNet service endpoints to only allow trusted client IPs or VNet ranges to connect.
Create indexes that match your aggregation pattern: add a compound index on (customerId, eventDate) to accelerate recency and frequency aggregations and to support sorts by eventDate per customer.
For category-affinity calculations, index the category field (or use a compound index with customerId if queries filter by both) so grouping/lookup by category is efficient.
When computing metrics that only need a subset of fields, always project to return only required fields in aggregation ($project or pipeline projection) to reduce IO and network transfer.
Use explain() or the MCP/monitoring tooling to verify aggregation query plans and confirm the aggregation uses the intended indexes; iterate index design based on actual query plans.
Handle transient errors (network blips, 429 RateLimit) by implementing retries with exponential backoff; respect server-provided Retry-After or equivalent headers when available.
When writing the assigned segment back to the customer document, perform an atomic update (updateOne with $set or findOneAndUpdate) rather than read-modify-write to avoid race conditions.

For stronger concurrency control when multiple agents may update the same profile, use optimistic concurrency (include a version field or etag and require it in the update filter) or use findOneAndUpdate with upsert=false and an appropriate filter.
Use bulk writes/inserts (ordered=false, bulk_write) when seeding or loading many events to dramatically improve ingestion throughput and reduce RU consumption.
Provision throughput and monitor RU/s consumption for the sample_customer_360_08 database; use autoscale or adjust RU allocation if aggregations or vector searches are causing throttling.
Use TTL indexes on the events collection for ephemeral or very old events (create a TTL index on the eventDate field) to automatically prune old documents and control storage/growth.
Limit aggregation result size and use server-side pagination for any query that may return many customers; avoid transferring huge result sets to the app in one call.

Cache segmentation rules in application memory and reload them only when changed (e.g., watch a config version field); do not read rules from DocumentDB on every prompt invocation to reduce latency and RU cost.

For vector search, ensure vectors are stored in a dedicated field with consistent dimensionality and normalized if using cosine similarity; create the appropriate vector index (HNSW/DiskANN/IVF) and set index parameters (M, efConstruction, efSearch) to match accuracy/latency needs.
When creating vector indexes, explicitly specify the distance metric (cosine, dot, or L2) consistent with how you compute/normalize vectors at query time to avoid mismatched results.
Monitor and rotate long-lived credentials regularly; when rotating keys, use a two-key rollover pattern so the app can switch without downtime.
Keep customer profile schema backward-compatible: store segment labels in a named field (e.g., segments.current and segments.history array with timestamps) instead of mutating unrelated fields.
Use unit and integration tests against a dedicated test database (e.g., sample_customer_360_08_test), seed known data, and clean up test documents; do not run tests against production clusters.
Instrument and log key metrics (RU consumption, latency, 429 rates, index usage) and include correlation IDs in logs so CLI and FastAPI requests can be traced to DB operations.

Avoid storing high-cardinality or unbounded arrays directly in the customer doc for frequently updated event data; keep events in a separate collection and compute metrics with aggregation or pre-aggregate into a summary collection to reduce hot documents and RU costs.
